subject: Archaeology
subcategory: Lost Cities of the Ancient World
title: Hampi: India's City of Riches
description: A fast breakdown of Hampi: India's City of Riches for builders.

hook.text: A city in India was once richer than Rome. When it fell, the victors spent six months looting it.

buildup.text: Hampi was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire in southern India, home to 500,000 people by the 1500s.

discovery.text: Portuguese traders described streets lined with gem merchants and markets selling Arabian horses.

twist.text: A coalition of Muslim sultanates defeated Vijayanagara in 1565 and systematically destroyed the city.

climax.text: Over 1,600 monuments survive among the boulder-strewn landscape — temples, bazaars, and royal elephant stables.

punchline.text: It took six months to destroy a city that took 200 years to build.

quiz.question: What happened to Hampi in 1565?
options: A massive flood from the river washed away most of the city
A coalition of sultanates defeated and systematically destroyed it
The ruling dynasty abandoned it to build a new capital

details.summary: Hampi in Karnataka, India, was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire from the 14th to 16th centuries — one of the wealthiest and largest cities in the medieval world, with a population estimated at 500,000. It was destroyed after the Battle of Talikota in 1565.
details.whyItMatters: Hampi's ruins reveal the grandeur of a major Indian empire that rivaled contemporary European states. Its destruction and subsequent neglect illustrate how quickly even the greatest cities can be reduced to picturesque ruins.
takeaways: Capital of the Vijayanagara Empire with an estimated 500,000 residents
One of the wealthiest medieval cities in the world
Sacked and destroyed after the Battle of Talikota in 1565

faq.question: How wealthy was Hampi at its peak?
faq.answer: Portuguese visitors described markets overflowing with diamonds, rubies, silks, and spices. The city controlled lucrative Indian Ocean trade networks. Its temples were covered in gold leaf. Foreign travelers compared it favorably to Rome and said it surpassed any European city they had seen.

faq.question: What happened at the Battle of Talikota?
faq.answer: In 1565, a coalition of Deccan sultanates defeated the Vijayanagara army. The victors spent months systematically destroying Hampi — pulling down buildings, smashing sculptures, and burning the city. The devastation was so complete that the site was never reoccupied as a capital.
